prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Edit the attached three-frame pixel-art brigand idle sheet. Keep the character design, muted six-color palette, solid navy hair, face, axe, shoulder twist, waist, legs and feet. Transparent background, three equal cells in one row, no text.
ADD A CLEAR DARK CHIN/JAW CONTOUR on EACH sprite: a SHORT thin curved stair-step line immediately under the jaw. Use the existing near-black navy #172638. It must define where the face ends and the neck begins. At the final 96px sprite size the line is only ONE pixel thick and about 6–8 pixels long, curving under the chin. It is NOT a thick straight horizontal stripe across the whole throat. Leave tan skin connected around the ends of the short jawline so the neck remains attached to the face. No choker, beard, floating head, or transparent gap. Do not remove the neck skin under this line.
MAKE THE NECK FOLLOW THE SMALL SHOULDER TURN: in pose0 the lower neck and collar lean very slightly toward the raised screen-right shoulder, pose1 return to center, pose2 the lower neck/collar lean slightly toward the raised screen-left shoulder. Upper jaw/head stay at the same screen center. The neck base shifts only one or two pixels at 96px output scale, with a continuous skin bridge. Show a small change in the SIDE neck contour and V-neck opening, not an overall head bob or whole-body sway.
The three existing poses stay distinct and keep their order. Keep all other anatomy and equipment as close as possible to the reference. Matte colors only, no hair/clothes highlights, no added props, floor, labels or borders.
integration: Only the authored jaw/neck/collar region is registered onto the previous accepted idle poses; surrounding art is preserved.
